cli.policy.title: READ-ONLY POLICY
cli.policy.intro: This tool only READS information from Windows for diagnosis. It never changes the registry, services, drivers or programs, and never runs repairs, cleanups or optimizations. The only permitted write is creating the diagnostic artifacts inside the output directory you authorize.
cli.policy.points: Nothing is installed, uninstalled, updated or terminated.
No service, scheduled task or startup entry is changed.
No repair check (chkdsk, sfc, dism) is executed.
This script sends no data to the internet. If an AI agent runs it for you, the agent reads the results and its AI service processes them.
Every command is statically verified against an allowlist before execution.

score.explanation: The score starts at 100 and is reduced only by substantiated findings, with penalties capped per category. Categories without base checks or without evidence are left out of the score instead of counting as healthy. Inconclusive, denied or unsupported checks do NOT reduce the score - and do not prove health either. Diagnostic risk is reported separately: high data confidence does not mean a healthy computer.
score.provisional.explain: Coverage or confidence is insufficient: treat this score as provisional. Missing data may be hiding problems.
score.unavailable.explain: Coverage is too low to compute a meaningful score. Run again in another session or grant the accesses listed under Limitations.

report.methodology.rules: Rules version: {0}. Deterministic score; weights configurable in rules/rules.json.
report.methodology.notes: The score starts at 100 and is reduced only by substantiated findings (state 'finding' with penalty > 0).
Category penalties are capped at the category weight; rules in the same dedupe group count once.
States unknown, access_denied, unsupported, not_collected and error never reduce the score.
The base metric uses the same central set of checks in Simple and Full modes; Full-only findings are additional analysis without penalty.
Insufficient coverage yields 'Provisional score' or 'Score unavailable' - never a reassuring 100/100.

report.methodology.states: Possible check states: OK, Finding, Inconclusive, Unsupported, Access denied, Not collected, Error.
report.methodology.disclaimer: The score is a review aid. It is not a medical diagnosis of the hardware, a warranty or a security certification.
report.review.title: How to review this report
report.review.steps: Start with 'Main findings' and read each item's 'Recommended human verification'.

If you want to discuss the findings with a trusted technician or an AI, that is optional and your decision: review the sanitized JSON first, because it can contain sensitive metadata. FIX MY PC sends nothing.
Compare cited events with Windows Event Viewer and with what you notice in real usage.
Nothing here authorizes automatic actions: any fix is your decision and execution.

rules.storage.smart_predict_failure.huma: Immediate backup and disk replacement are the usual actions; confirm with the vendor's tool.

rules.storage.disk_event_errors.detail: Error events from storage components in the last {1} h: {0}. This does not prove a physical defect: Volsnap events, for example, usually reflect the shadow-copy (restore point) space limit, not a disk failure.
rules.storage.disk_event_errors.humanChe: Correlate with perceived freezes or slowness; a technician can inspect the cited event details.

rules.events.critical_recurring.detail: {0} occurrences of provider '{1}' (ID {2}) in log {3}, recorded within the last 48 h.
rules.events.critical_recurring.humanChe: Open Event Viewer, filter by the cited ID and check whether the problem matches real symptoms.

rules.events.error_concentration.detail: {0} occurrences of provider '{1}' (ID {2}) recently - worth reviewing that specific cause.
rules.events.error_concentration.humanCh: Research the cited provider/ID; one noisy component usually points to a specific problem.

rules.events.whea_hardware.detail: {0} WHEA-Logger event(s) in the last 7 days.

rules.events.unexpected_shutdown.detail: {0} unexpected shutdown(s) in the last 7 days (Kernel-Power 41 / EventLog 6008).
rules.events.unexpected_shutdown.humanCh: If there was a power outage or forced power-off it may be benign; recurrence without apparent cause deserves a power-supply check.
rules.events.bsod.title: Severe system failures (blue screen)
rules.events.bsod.detail: {0} BugCheck record(s) in the last 7 days.
rules.events.bsod.humanCheck: Note the stop code when it happens; drivers and memory are the most common causes - a technician can analyze the minidump.

rules.perf.cpu_sustained_high.humanCheck: Repeat the observation during normal use; only if it persists, identify the consuming process in Task Manager.

rules.perf.commit_pressure.humanCheck: If recurrent, consider closing programs or adding RAM; a single reading proves nothing by itself.

rules.os.long_uptime.title: System up for a long time
rules.os.long_uptime.humanCheck: Rebooting applies pending updates; no fault is associated with this finding.
rules.startup.unsigned_autostart.title: Unsigned startup executables
rules.startup.unsigned_autostart.humanCh: A missing signature is NOT proof of malware - legitimate tools ship unsigned too. Identify the program before any decision.

report.summary.coverage.note: Coverage is how much of the applicable checks produced usable evidence. It is not a health indicator: a complete audit can still find problems, and a partial one can hide them.
report.summary.analysisOnlyCount: Additional analysis (Full mode, outside the base score): {0}
report.score.noGauge: No gauge is shown because a score could not be computed from the available evidence.
report.score.scale: Scale from 0 to 100. A higher value means fewer substantiated findings; it does not certify the PC.
report.score.provisionalNote: No problem was found in the checks that completed (coverage {0}). This does not prove the PC is healthy.
report.findings.lead: Ordered by the severity assigned by the rules, then by score impact. Severity and confidence come from the deterministic rules; they are not a verdict on the hardware or on security.
report.finding.noLimitations: No specific limitation recorded for this finding.
report.perf.sampling: Memory and processes are a single snapshot taken during collection, and CPU is a short sample. None of this shows long-term behavior.
report.startup.counts: {0} registry/folder entries, {1} scheduled tasks, {2} automatic services.
report.startup.unknownNote: An unfamiliar name or a missing signature is not evidence of a problem; many legitimate tools look unfamiliar. Confirm what an item is before acting on it.
report.events.historicalNote: These are historical records from the analysis window. A past event does not mean the problem is still present.
report.events.truncatedNote: At least one log reached the read limit: counts marked with + are lower bounds.
report.privacy.points: This audit only reads information. It does not change Windows and does not install, remove or repair anything.
The report can still contain private information (device names, installed software, dates). Review it before sharing.

The sanitized JSON is the better version if you decide to share with a reviewer or an AI assistant. Sharing is optional, nothing is sent automatically and anonymization is not perfect: review the file first. The internal JSON, if you generated it, stays on this computer.
Sanitization masks known sensitive fields but cannot guarantee that a computer or person can never be identified from what remains.
Inconclusive items need confirmation by a person before any conclusion is drawn.
Any fix is a separate decision: evaluate each one on its own, with a backup, before acting.

diag.symptom.boot: The computer takes long to start
diag.symptom.slow: The computer gets slow during use
diag.symptom.crash: The computer freezes or restarts unexpectedly
diag.conclusion.found: We found evidence that may be related to the reported problem. It shows where to look, but on its own it does not confirm the cause.
diag.conclusion.weak: We found partial or indirect signs related to the reported problem. None of them explains the symptom on its own.
diag.conclusion.none: Under the conditions checked, we found no evidence related to the reported problem. This does not rule out an intermittent problem or one that happens outside the measurement window.
diag.conclusion.insufficient: We could not check enough data to answer about the reported problem. See below what could not be verified.
diag.state.unknown: no conclusion is possible from the available data
diag.state.not_collected: not checked in this audit mode
diag.state.access_denied: Windows denied access to this source without administrator rights
diag.state.unsupported: source not available in this Windows version or configuration
diag.state.partial_unknown: Windows reports the disks as healthy, but SMART data could not be verified
diag.q.cpu_load.label: CPU load
diag.q.cpu_load.title: Processor busy during the measurement
diag.q.cpu_load.yes: CPU usage reached {highPct}% or higher in {highSharePct}% of valid samples (average {avg}%, peak {max}%) in the {window} s window. Processes with high usage in their observed intervals: {processes}.
diag.q.cpu_load.partial: There were CPU peaks (maximum {max}%), but the load did not stay high: average {avg}%, above {highPct}% in {highSharePct}% of the samples.
diag.q.cpu_load.no: The CPU was not saturated during the measurement: average {avg}%, peak {max}%.
diag.f.cpu_load.why: A processor that is busy almost all the time makes programs slower to respond. High load is also normal during updates, builds, games or antivirus scans.
diag.f.cpu_load.action: Repeat the measurement while the slowness happens and check in Task Manager which processes are at the top. If it is always the same program, check with its vendor.
diag.q.memory_pressure.label: Memory pressure
diag.q.memory_pressure.title: Little memory available during the measurement
diag.q.memory_pressure.yes: Available memory stayed low (average {availAvgMB} MB, minimum {availMinMB} MB) with signs of paging ({pagesAvg} pages read from disk per second on average) or high commit (maximum {commitMax}%).
diag.q.memory_pressure.partial: Some measurements suggested memory pressure (average available memory {availAvgMB} MB, page reads {pagesAvg}/s, peak commit {commitMax}%).
diag.q.memory_pressure.no: Available memory stayed adequate (average {availAvgMB} MB, minimum {availMinMB} MB), without relevant paging.
diag.f.memory_pressure.why: When available memory runs short, Windows reads data back from disk (paging), which can make responses slower. A short measurement does not show a memory leak.
diag.f.memory_pressure.action: Check in Task Manager (Performance > Memory) how much stays available with your usual programs open. If it is often low, close what you are not using; consider more memory only if this keeps happening.
diag.q.storage_busy.label: Busy disk
diag.q.storage_busy.title: Storage very busy
diag.q.storage_busy.yes: The average queue for disk {disk} reached the threshold in the measurement window (average {queueAvg}, maximum {queueMax}, throughput {mbPerSec} MB/s).
diag.q.storage_busy.partial: The queue for disk {disk} reached the peak threshold (maximum {queueMax}, average {queueAvg}).
diag.q.storage_busy.no: The measured queues stayed below the thresholds (highest average queue of {queueAvg} on disk {disk}).
diag.f.storage_busy.why: Queued requests can make other programs wait. Updates, sync, indexing and antivirus can also create queues.
diag.f.storage_busy.action: Check in Task Manager (Processes, Disk column) which programs read or write the most. Repeat the measurement at another time to see whether the activity recurs.
diag.q.storage_slow.label: Disk response time
diag.q.storage_slow.title: Storage responding slowly
diag.q.storage_slow.yes: Disk {disk} responded slowly: average read time {readAvgMs} ms and write time {writeAvgMs} ms (review reference: {highMs} ms).
diag.q.storage_slow.partial: Disk {disk} responded slowly during part of the measurement (p90 {p90Ms} ms; average read {readAvgMs} ms, average write {writeAvgMs} ms).
diag.q.storage_slow.no: Storage response times stayed low during the measurement (worst case: read {readAvgMs} ms and write {writeAvgMs} ms on disk {disk}).
diag.f.storage_slow.why: High response times make each read or write take longer, which slows the computer even with an idle CPU. The right value differs between NVMe SSDs, SATA, hard drives and virtual disks.
diag.f.storage_slow.action: Compare response times in Resource Monitor and repeat the measurement under light use. If the delay persists, check the disk's reported health.
diag.q.storage_errors.label: Historical disk errors
diag.q.storage_errors.title: Storage errors recorded by Windows
diag.q.storage_errors.yes: Windows recorded disk or file system errors in the last {recentHours} h ({items}).
diag.q.storage_errors.partial: Windows recorded disk or file system errors in the last {recentHours} h ({items}).
diag.q.storage_errors.no: No disk or file system errors were recorded in the last {recentHours} h.
diag.f.storage_errors.why: Recorded disk errors can point to connection, file system or disk problems. An old, isolated event does not always mean a current failure.
diag.f.storage_errors.action: Back up important files and check in Event Viewer whether the errors keep appearing. If they recur, consult a technician or the manufacturer's tool.
diag.q.storage_health.label: Physical storage health
diag.q.storage_health.title: Disk health reported by Windows
diag.q.storage_health.yes: Windows reports a failure or a predicted failure on at least one disk.
diag.q.storage_health.partial: Windows reports a failure or a predicted failure on at least one disk.
diag.q.storage_health.no: Windows reports the disks as healthy (SMART read state: {smart}).
diag.f.storage_health.why: Windows itself (or the disk's SMART) reported a failure or predicted failure. This is the strongest data-risk signal this tool can observe.
diag.f.storage_health.action: Back up your files as soon as possible and have a technician assess the disk.
diag.q.boot_history.label: Boot history
diag.q.boot_history.title: Slow boots recorded by Windows
diag.q.boot_history.yes: Across {boots} recorded boots ({windowDays} days), the median time to the desktop was {medianMainPathSec} s and Windows flagged {degraded} as degraded. Median total time: {medianBootSec} s (from {minSec} to {maxSec} s). Components flagged more than once: {contributors}.
diag.q.boot_history.partial: Across {boots} recorded boots, the median time to the desktop was {medianMainPathSec} s and {degraded} was flagged as degraded. The signal is moderate. Components flagged more than once: {contributors}.
diag.q.boot_history.no: Across {boots} recorded boots, the median time to the desktop was {medianMainPathSec} s, with no recurring degradation flagged by Windows.
diag.f.boot_history.why: Windows times every boot and flags the ones slower than usual. These records show whether the delay recurs and sometimes which components added to it.
diag.f.boot_history.action: Compare the delay you notice with the recorded times. If a component appears repeatedly, check whether you still need it or whether the vendor has an update. Do not disable items without knowing what they do.
diag.q.crash_history.label: Freezes and restarts
diag.q.crash_history.title: Unexpected restarts or recorded failures
diag.q.crash_history.yes: In the last {windowDays} days there were {restarts} unexpected restart(s) on {restartDays} different day(s) and {bugchecks} recorded blue screen(s). Last unexpected restart: {lastRestart}. Event 41 context: {withBugcheck} preceded by a recorded stop error (blue screen) and {withPowerButton} with the power button held down.
diag.q.crash_history.partial: The last {windowDays} days showed signs of instability ({restarts} unexpected restart(s), {bugchecks} blue screen(s), {whea} reported hardware error(s), {appCrashes} application crash(es), {appHangs} application hang(s), {serviceCrashes} service failure(s)).
diag.q.crash_history.no: No unexpected restart or blue screen was recorded in the last {windowDays} days.
diag.f.crash_history.why: Repeated unexpected restarts confirm abnormal interruptions but do not identify the cause on their own: power loss, a held power button, drivers, overheating or hardware are all possible.
diag.f.crash_history.action: Open Windows Reliability Monitor to see the event timeline and note what was happening before each restart. If blue screens repeat, take the dates to a technician.
diag.rule.why: This finding comes from FIX MY PC's deterministic rules and applies whatever symptom was reported.
diag.lim.window_only: Applies only to the measured window; intermittent problems outside it do not show up.
diag.lim.snapshot_only: The Quick audit has only a short reading (about 4 seconds), which cannot show behavior over time.
diag.lim.standby_is_available: Cached and standby memory counts as available: it is not waste.
diag.lim.busy_not_fault: A busy disk is not a defect; it may be legitimate work.
diag.lim.latency_no_universal: There is no universal latency limit: NVMe, SATA, hard drives and virtual disks behave differently.
diag.lim.history_not_current: Historical event: it does not prove the problem is still present.
diag.lim.history_incomplete: Part of the System or Application history was unavailable or reached the collection limit. Counts reflect the records that were read.
diag.lim.health_is_reported: This is the state reported by Windows and the disk, not a physical test.
diag.lim.smart_unavailable: SMART data could not be read; physical health was not verified.
diag.lim.boot_log_admin: The Windows boot performance log is usually readable only by administrators; the tool does not request elevation.
diag.lim.boot_no_events: Windows recorded no boot timing events in the period.
diag.lim.boot_phases: Time to the desktop (MainPath) and time until the system goes idle (PostBoot) are Windows measurements and may differ from what you notice; time spent at the password screen is not counted.
diag.lim.startup_count_not_cause: The number of startup programs alone does not explain the delay.
diag.lim.kp41_not_psu: Kernel-Power event 41 means Windows was not shut down cleanly; it does not prove a power supply defect.
diag.alt.legit_load: It may be legitimate work: updates, builds, games, video or an antivirus scan.
diag.alt.background_tasks: Windows maintenance tasks run in the background at varying times.
diag.alt.many_apps: Many programs or tabs open at the same time.
diag.alt.short_window_leak: A process growing in memory over a short time does not show a leak.
diag.alt.legit_io: Cloud sync, indexing, backup or an update writing to disk.
diag.alt.heavy_io: Large file copies raise response times temporarily.
diag.alt.virtual_disk: On virtual machines or RAID controllers the counters may not reflect the physical disk.
diag.alt.cable_or_removable: Cables, USB ports and removable drives also produce these errors.
diag.alt.after_update: Boots right after updates are usually slower.
diag.alt.perceived_vs_measured: The delay you notice may come after the desktop appears, while programs are still opening.
diag.alt.power_loss: Power loss or a held power button.
diag.next.reproduce: Repeat the Full audit while the slowness is happening, so the problem is measured when it occurs.
diag.next.full_audit: Run the Full audit: it observes the computer for longer and checks the history related to the symptom.
diag.next.full_for_symptom: If there is a specific problem (slowness, slow startup or crashes), run the Full audit and choose that symptom.
diag.next.boot_admin: To check the boot history, an administrator can open Event Viewer at Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Diagnostics-Performance > Operational (read-only).
diag.next.reliability_monitor: Open Reliability Monitor (search for “reliability” in the Start menu) to see the events by date.
diag.next.backup: Back up important files before doing anything else.
diag.next.smart_vendor: The disk's physical health could not be verified: use the disk manufacturer's tool if you want to confirm it.
diag.next.note_when: Note when the problem happens (time, open program, what you were doing). It helps repeat the measurement at the right moment.

diag.q.process_commit.label: Committed memory per process
diag.q.process_commit.title: Process with a lot of committed memory
diag.q.process_commit.yes: {name} holds {commitMB} MB of committed private memory (Working Set {workingSetMB} MB) and the system showed signs of memory pressure. Change of {growthMB} MB in {window} s. Largest: {processes}.
diag.q.process_commit.partial: {name} holds {commitMB} MB of committed private memory (Working Set {workingSetMB} MB), with no system memory pressure during the measurement. Change of {growthMB} MB in {window} s. Largest: {processes}.
diag.q.process_commit.no: No process exceeded {highMB} MB of committed private memory. Largest: {processes}.
diag.f.process_commit.why: Committed memory counts toward the Windows commit limit even when it is not in RAM, so it can be high while the Working Set is low.
diag.f.process_commit.action: In Task Manager, Details tab, add the “Commit size” column and follow {name} during normal use. If the value only grows for hours, look for a program update or contact its vendor.
diag.f.process_commit.hypothesis: {name} may be contributing to the use of the Windows memory limit. A single measurement does not demonstrate a leak.
diag.q.process_io.label: I/O per process
diag.q.process_io.title: Processes doing I/O while the disk was busy
diag.q.process_io.yes: With the disk busy or slow, {name} had the highest observed I/O ({mbPerSec} MB/s, {sharePct}% of process I/O). Largest (read/write): {processes}.
diag.q.process_io.partial: With partial signs of a busy or slow disk, {name} had the highest observed I/O ({mbPerSec} MB/s, {sharePct}% of process I/O). Largest (read/write): {processes}.
diag.q.process_io.no: Process I/O did not coincide with a busy or slow disk. Largest: {name} ({mbPerSec} MB/s).
diag.f.process_io.why: Knowing who did I/O in the same period helps choose what to watch. It is a coincidence in time, not an attribution of the disk load.
diag.f.process_io.action: Open Resource Monitor, Disk tab, while the problem happens and check whether {name} shows disk activity. If it is an expected task, wait for it to finish before judging.
diag.f.process_io.hypothesis: Activity from {name} may be contributing to the disk load.
diag.q.graphics_events.label: Graphics driver events
diag.q.graphics_events.title: Graphics driver events recorded
diag.q.graphics_events.yes: Windows recorded {count} graphics events on {days} day(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}); {paired} of them with a matching event within 120 s. Latest: {last}.
diag.q.graphics_events.partial: Windows recorded {count} isolated graphics event(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}). Latest: {last}.
diag.q.graphics_events.no: No graphics event from the catalog in the last {windowDays} days.
diag.f.graphics_events.why: These records say the display driver stopped responding or reported an error. The reason can be the driver, an application, the configuration or the hardware.
diag.f.graphics_events.action: Compare the times with the freezes you noticed. Check the GPU vendor's site for a newer driver and, if the problem follows one game or program, test without it.
diag.f.graphics_events.hypothesis: Instability was recorded in the graphics subsystem. The events do not demonstrate a physical GPU defect.
diag.q.storage_signals.label: Storage signals
diag.q.storage_signals.title: Storage warnings and errors recorded
diag.q.storage_signals.yes: Windows recorded {count} storage signals on {days} day(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}). Latest: {last}.
diag.q.storage_signals.partial: Windows recorded {count} isolated storage signal(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}). Latest: {last}.
diag.q.storage_signals.no: No storage warning or error from the catalog in the last {windowDays} days.
diag.f.storage_signals.why: I/O retries and controller resets show the path to the disk had trouble at that moment. They can come from a cable, port, power, driver or the drive itself.
diag.f.storage_signals.action: Keep a current backup. Check the drive's health with the vendor's tool and, for external or removable disks, try another cable or port.
diag.f.storage_signals.hypothesis: The storage path may be unstable. These events alone do not prove a physical disk failure.
diag.q.network_ports.label: Port exhaustion (history)
diag.q.network_ports.title: Port exhaustion recorded in history
diag.q.network_ports.yes: Windows recorded {count} port exhaustion events on {days} day(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}). Latest: {last}. Current port use was not measured.
diag.q.network_ports.partial: Windows recorded {count} isolated port exhaustion event(s) in the last {windowDays} days ({items}). Latest: {last}. Current port use was not measured.
diag.q.network_ports.no: No port exhaustion event in the last {windowDays} days.
diag.f.network_ports.why: When ephemeral ports run out, new connections fail for a while. The record is historical and does not identify the responsible program.
diag.f.network_ports.action: If connection failures return, note the time and run a new audit with it. Also note which programs were open at that moment.
diag.f.network_ports.hypothesis: A program may have opened too many connections at those moments. This does not mean the problem is active now.
diag.q.incident_correlation.label: Events near the reported time
diag.q.incident_correlation.title: Events recorded near the time of the problem
diag.q.incident_correlation.yes: Near {when} there are {faults} fault event(s), from: {families}. Closest: {closest}.
diag.q.incident_correlation.partial: Near {when} there are only routine startup or shutdown records. Closest: {closest}.
diag.f.incident_correlation.why: Being close to the reported time helps choose what to investigate first, but two nearby records are not causally related for that reason.
diag.f.incident_correlation.action: Check the closest events in the report timeline and whether the reported time is right. If the problem returns, note the exact time.
diag.f.incident_correlation.hypothesis: The closest events are the first candidates to investigate for this episode. None of them was confirmed as the cause.
diag.f.cpu_load.hypothesis: CPU load may be contributing to the slowness you noticed.
diag.f.memory_pressure.hypothesis: Lack of available memory may be contributing to the slowness.
diag.f.storage_busy.hypothesis: Disk load may be contributing to the slowness. This does not indicate a defect.
diag.f.storage_slow.hypothesis: Slow storage responses may be contributing to the slowness. Slowness alone does not indicate a physical failure.
diag.f.storage_errors.hypothesis: The recorded errors may relate to a cable, removable device, driver or the drive.
diag.f.storage_health.hypothesis: The drive may be reporting a health problem.
diag.f.boot_history.hypothesis: Startup components or updates may have lengthened boot time.
diag.f.crash_history.hypothesis: There are signs of instability. The records alone do not identify the responsible part or software.
diag.lim.commit_not_leak: High committed memory in one measurement does not demonstrate a leak: confirming it requires following the process for longer.
diag.lim.commit_unavailable: Windows did not report committed memory for the observed processes.
diag.lim.commit_low_resident: Most of this memory is not resident in RAM; looking only at the Working Set would hide this usage.
diag.lim.io_not_only_disk: Per-process I/O counters include files, network and devices, and the cache can serve reads without touching the disk.
diag.lim.retention_short: The log does not reach the whole window; no events in the older period proves nothing.
diag.lim.catalog_truncated: The record limit was reached; the oldest occurrences were not read and the count is a minimum.
diag.lim.graphics_not_hardware: Graphics driver events do not prove a physical GPU defect.
diag.lim.storage_signal_not_failure: Storage warnings do not prove a physical failure; cables, ports, power and drivers produce the same records.
diag.lim.ports_history_only: These events are historical: the current port state and the responsible program were not checked.
diag.lim.incident_proximity: Proximity in time does not demonstrate cause.
diag.lim.incident_ambiguous: The reported local time repeats at the end of daylight saving time; the search covers both possibilities.
diag.lim.incident_no_catalog: The event catalog was not collected in this audit, so the time could not be compared.
diag.lim.incident_after_run: The reported time is after the end of the audit; no correlation was made.
diag.lim.incident_clock_future: There are events dated after the end of the audit, a sign of an inconsistent clock; no correlation was made.
diag.lim.incident_clock_step: The system clock was changed near that time; distances between events are not reliable and no correlation was made.
diag.lim.incident_before_retention: The log does not reach that time: the events from that moment no longer exist.
diag.lim.incident_partial_retention: The log reaches only part of the window around that time.
diag.lim.incident_retention_unknown: It was not possible to tell how far back the log reaches; no correlation was made.
diag.alt.commit_reserved: Some programs reserve committed memory without actually using it.
diag.alt.io_network_cache: Part of this I/O may be network, devices or reads served from cache.
diag.alt.graphics_app: A specific game or program may have triggered the graphics event.
diag.alt.storage_driver: A controller driver or firmware can produce these records.
diag.alt.port_heavy_app: Programs with many short connections can temporarily exhaust ports.
diag.alt.coincidence: The events may have happened near that time by coincidence.

diag.q.graphics_timeout.label: Graphics timeout
diag.q.graphics_timeout.title: Windows recorded a display driver timeout
diag.q.graphics_timeout.yes: There are {liveKernel} kernel video timeout report(s) ({codes}) on {days} day(s); {paired} of them within {windowSec} s of a driver event (the closest {closestSec} s apart).
diag.q.graphics_timeout.partial: There are isolated signs: {driverEvents} driver event(s) and {liveKernel} kernel video timeout report(s), with no close match in time.
diag.q.graphics_timeout.no: No video timeout was found in Windows reports or driver events.
diag.f.graphics_timeout.why: When the display driver takes too long to respond, Windows tries to recover it; this can show up as a brief black screen or a momentary freeze.
diag.f.graphics_timeout.action: Next time, note the time and run FIX MY PC with it. Check the GPU vendor's site for a newer driver and whether the problem follows one game or program.
diag.f.graphics_timeout.hypothesis: There may be instability in the display driver, in an application using the GPU, or in the card itself. The records do not identify which.
diag.q.wer_failures.label: Windows failure reports
diag.q.wer_failures.title: New failures recorded by Windows
diag.q.wer_failures.yes: Windows has {reports} failure report(s), {newRecent} new in the last {recentHours} h. Of {records} records, {resends} are re-sends. Types: {appCrash} application crash(es), {appHang} hang(s), {liveKernel} kernel event(s), {blueScreen} blue screen(s).
diag.q.wer_failures.partial: Windows has {reports} failure report(s), none confirmed as new in the last {recentHours} h. Of {records} records, {resends} are re-sends; {resendRecent} older report(s) were re-sent in that period. Types: {appCrash} application crash(es), {appHang} hang(s), {liveKernel} kernel event(s), {blueScreen} blue screen(s).
diag.q.wer_failures.no: No Windows failure report in the period read.
diag.f.wer_failures.why: Each report stands for one failure. Windows can write the same report several times while trying to send it, and those re-sends are not new failures.
diag.f.wer_failures.action: Open Reliability Monitor and see whether the failures concentrate on one program. Update that program before investigating the rest of the system.
diag.f.wer_failures.hypothesis: One or more programs or components failed recently. The reports do not demonstrate the cause of the failure.
diag.q.ports_current.label: Current port use
diag.q.ports_current.title: High port use right now
diag.q.ports_current.yes: There are {inUse} active TCP connections, about {usagePct}% of the dynamic range of {rangeSize} ports. Trend during the measurement: {trend}. Largest owners now: {owners}.
diag.q.ports_current.partial: There are {inUse} active TCP connections, about {usagePct}% of the dynamic range of {rangeSize} ports. Trend during the measurement: {trend}. Largest owners now: {owners}.
diag.q.ports_current.no: Current port use is normal: {inUse} active TCP connections, about {usagePct}% of the range of {rangeSize}. Trend during the measurement: {trend}.
diag.f.ports_current.why: If ephemeral ports run out, new connections fail. The measurement shows the current moment and does not reveal who caused past episodes.
diag.f.ports_current.action: If connections are failing now, check in Resource Monitor, Network tab, whether one of the listed programs holds many connections. Closing and reopening the program is a safe check.
diag.f.ports_current.hypothesis: A program may be holding too many connections right now.
diag.q.storage_device.label: Disk in the events
diag.q.storage_device.title: Disk associated with storage events
diag.q.storage_device.yes: Disk events point to {disks}; {currentBoot} disk(s) have events since the last boot.
diag.q.storage_device.partial: Disk events point to {disks}, but none since the last boot: {earlier} disk(s) may have changed number and {absent} no longer exist.
diag.q.storage_device.no: No disk event identifies a device.
diag.h.graphics_driver_instability: Display driver or graphics subsystem instability
diag.lim.wer_time_upper: A report's time is when it was written; the failure may have happened earlier.
diag.lim.wer_truncated: The record limit was reached; older reports were not read and the counts are a minimum.
diag.lim.wer_unavailable: Windows failure reports could not be read.
diag.lim.wer_unidentified: Some records had no readable identifier and were not counted as reports.
diag.lim.ports_approximate: Occupancy is approximate: it counts active connections without reading each one's port.
diag.lim.ports_owner_history: The program responsible for a past exhaustion cannot be identified after the fact.
diag.lim.ports_range_varies: Network profiles have different ranges; the smallest was used.
diag.lim.disk_number_boot: A disk's number can change between boots; older events may refer to another device.
diag.sup.service_hosts: Services in svchost processes among the top consumers: {hosts}. A shared process does not allow splitting usage per service.
diag.sup.gpu_use: GPU use at the time of the audit: {gpu}.
diag.sup.storage_reliability: Total read/write errors reported by the disks: {disks}. The counters have no dates.
diag.sup.confirm_sustained: A second measurement confirmed the signal continuously.
diag.sup.confirm_recurring: A second measurement showed new peaks, without continuous load.
diag.sup.confirm_isolated: A second measurement did not repeat the peak; it may have been isolated.

report.hyp.title: Hypotheses evaluated
report.hyp.col.name: Hypothesis

report.wer.title: Windows failure reports
report.wer.note: Each unique report is one failure. Repeated records of the same report are re-sends. The time is when it was written, which can be after the failure.
report.gpu.title: Video: GPU and drivers
report.gpu.note: A few seconds of measurement, at the time of the audit. Temperature, power and clocks were not checked because they need a vendor tool.

report.net.note: Counts only: addresses and ports are not read. Owners are the current ones and do not show who caused a past exhaustion. A measurement of seconds does not predict exhaustion.
report.svc.title: Services in svchost
report.svc.note: When several services share a process, usage cannot be attributed to one of them.
report.diskmap.title: Disks named in the events
report.diskmap.note: A disk's number can change between boots. Only events since the last boot are safely associated with the current disk.
report.rel.title: Disk reliability
report.rel.note: Values reported by the disk itself, without dates. Not every model reports every field, and reading them usually needs administrator rights.
